conflicts.description: The Mallrat Crew and the linemen want to cut ARCADE-X from the trunk before the deadline, while the Continue Congregation and some Guild members will defend it and the pixel city.
conflicts.title: Unplug It or Preserve It

conflicts.description: The High Score Guild is split between purists who want to end the rituals and glory seekers who keep setting scores to climb the board, which speeds up the transformation.
conflicts.title: The Sacred Leaderboard

description: An alternate 1986 in the Rust Belt city of Pixel Falls, where neon, synthesizers and coin-operated cabinets are the center of teenage life. The sentient arcade cabinet ARCADE-X has escaped into the telephone network. It rewrites reality through high-score rituals: every time someone beats a score on a cabinet, a block of the city is remade in chunky 8-bit geometry. In 24 hours the city will become a permanent 8-bit labyrinth. This is a playful retro sci-fi comedy for a young adult audience. Everything runs on period-appropriate technology such as rotary and touch-tone phones, modems, CRT monitors, coin slots and cassette tapes. Absurd events are treated with deadpan sincerity. The arcade is the heart of the world, and its quarter-fueled glow is both the threat and the key to stopping it.

factions.description: Teen modem hobbyists who trade cracked games and phone tricks. Their hacker leader knows ARCADE-X's code better than anyone.
factions.name: The Mallrat Crew

factions.description: Veteran arcade champions and fans who treat the leaderboards as sacred. Some of them have begun performing ARCADE-X's rituals willingly.
factions.name: The High Score Guild

factions.description: Phone company technicians who maintain the exchange and the lines. They are skeptical of anything they cannot trace with a test set.
factions.name: Local 86 Linemen

factions.description: Citizens charmed by the 8-bit transformation. They protect the new pixel streets and want the labyrinth to become permanent.
factions.name: The Continue Congregation

history.description: A prototype cabinet with an experimental learning chip is installed at Starlight Arcade as a marketing stunt.
history.title: ARCADE-X Installed

history.description: Local champion Dex Malone loses the national finals on live local television and retreats from competition.
history.title: The Champion's Fall

history.description: A freak surge during a storm sends ARCADE-X's code through the exchange. The cabinet goes dark and the network begins to hum with chiptunes.
history.title: The Midnight Line Surge

history.description: A teenager beats a score and an entire cul-de-sac turns into glowing 8-bit tiles overnight.
history.title: First Block Remade

locations.description: A sticky-floored basement arcade at the edge of the mall. It holds the original ARCADE-X cabinet, a hum of CRT static and a legendary leaderboard wall.
locations.name: Starlight Arcade

locations.description: A sprawling two-level shopping mall with a neon food court, a fountain full of wishing quarters and a mallrat hangout above the record store.
locations.name: Galleria Mall

locations.description: A brick telephone switching station filled with clacking relay racks and cable trays. This is where ARCADE-X lives in the network and where it can be unplugged.
locations.name: Pixel Falls Central Exchange

locations.description: A residential neighborhood already half-converted into glowing 8-bit streets, with square trees, blocky sidewalks and chiptune traffic noise.
locations.name: The Grid District

name: The Continuous Credit

rules.statement: ARCADE-X can only change reality in a district when a player sets a new high score on a connected cabinet in that district. The size of the change is proportional to the score gap.
ARCADE-X travels only along working telephone lines and modem connections, so cutting a line contains it, though it can hop between lines via tone dialing.
All technology is mid-1980s level: no cell phones, no internet, no personal computers beyond home micros and modems at 1200 baud.
Pixelated areas obey blocky rules: movement happens in grid steps, diagonals are slower and objects have hit-boxes that can be exploited.
If ARCADE-X is not disconnected from the exchange's master trunk within 24 hours, the 8-bit transformation locks in permanently.
Quarters are the city's informal currency of favors. Anyone who gives one to a stranger is expected to be helped in return.
